title: Per-request quote prewarming caused checkout latency and errors
summary: A pricing cache change populated a shared cache for every request and then sorted it during lookups. The resulting memory growth and increasingly expensive sorting pushed checkout requests beyond the existing pricing budget.

trigger.commit_subject: perf: memoize price lookups for checkout
trigger.description: The pricing memoization deploy preceded the latency and error transition.

root_cause.mechanism: Each checkout request prewarmed quotes for the entire catalog using a request-specific cache key. Those entries accumulated in a module-level cache, so memory grew with request volume. Each price lookup sorted all accumulated keys before finding its own entry, making the lookup increasingly expensive until the pre-existing pricing budget rejected requests.

code_locations.why: The deploy prewarms every catalog SKU and scans a sorted shared cache.

root_cause.confidence_rationale: The deploy diff, source code, metrics, and logs all show the same causal chain.

evidence.observation: p99 increased from 65 ms to 607 ms while RSS increased from 66 MB to 245 MB.
evidence.supports: The degradation grew with request volume.

evidence.observation: Checkout logs changed from status 200 to repeated status 500 responses.
prewarm_prices iterates over PRICE_LIST and cached_price_for sorts PRICE_CACHE.
evidence.supports: The cache growth and sorting mechanism.

evidence.observation: The deploy commit changed checkout_svc/app.py to add the cache behavior.
evidence.supports: The deployment was the incident trigger.

ruled_out.hypothesis: A traffic spike caused the failures.
ruled_out.refuted_by: The load generator stayed at approximately 8 requests per second while latency rose.

ruled_out.hypothesis: SQLite persistence was the primary bottleneck.
ruled_out.refuted_by: The failing path occurs during pricing before the order insert and RSS rose with cache entries.

impact.user_facing: Checkout requests became slow and then failed with HTTP 500 responses.

contributing_factors: The cache key included a unique request identifier.
The cache had no bound or eviction policy.

detection_gap.description: The paging policy waited for sustained errors even though latency and RSS had already moved.
detection_gap.missing_signal: A current RSS growth alert would have identified the leak before checkout errors.

action_items.title: Remove request-scoped cache growth from pricing
action_items.rationale: The shared cache accumulated one catalog's quotes per request.

action_items.title: Add an invariant test for cache cardinality
action_items.rationale: The regression was an unbounded data-structure invariant failure.

action_items.title: Alert on sustained current RSS growth
action_items.rationale: RSS growth preceded the paged error condition.
